battle.name: 法國二月革命
battle.brief: 一八四八年二月，巴黎國民國民衛隊與街壘武裝先後跟王朝軍隊交火，二月廿四日杜伊勒里宮被衝破，路易·菲利浦出逃，共和政府當夜在市政廳宣告成立。工人武裝三月在聖安東尼區築起街壘，四月選舉建立第二共和國，六月工業界再起而遭軍方槍決。兩邊的骨幹都是雷管步槍。

kit.name: 雷管步槍
kit.history: 雷管取代火燧之後，底火在霧裡也打得響。射程變長，隊形就散了。

countries: 交戰的一方是路易·菲利浦的七月王朝：常備軍約一萬人分駐巴黎與凡爾賽，內政大臣貝多掌巴黎防務，騎兵總監比約在革命爆發時還只是戰爭大臣，另有外省國家衛隊奉命北上。國王的權力支柱其實是巴黎國民衛隊，但它在二月二十二日前後分成資產階級營與工人營，兩派武裝互相猜疑，革命正是從這道裂縫鑽進去。另一方是共和派主導的巴黎起義者：民兵各街區營、行會武裝、外省湧來的農工、回國的法國流亡者，以及四月選舉後才掌權的共和派。關鍵人物包括總理大臣基佐、巴黎駐軍總指揮貝多、國民衛隊總指揮拉莫里西耶爾與其砲兵指揮佩迪耶。二月二十四日之後成立的臨時政府由杜邦·德·勒爾、克雷米歐、阿拉戈、拉馬丁、杜富爾、貝多、卡瓦IGNAC等人組成，六月鎮壓之後實際掌權的則是卡瓦IGNAC，他以陸軍步兵與要塞砲兵接管了巴黎的街壘。
countriesEn: The two sides in this conflict were the July Monarchy of Louis-Philippe and the Paris uprising that grew out of the National Guard. The royal side fielded roughly ten thousand regulars, most of them in or around Paris, with the interior minister Bedeau in charge of the city's defences and Marshal Bugeaud directing the cavalry and briefly serving as minister of war; battalions of the departmental National Guard were also ordered north. The crown's real pillar was the National Guard of Paris, yet that force split along class lines into bourgeois and worker battalions, and the revolution moved precisely into that fissure. On the other side stood republican-led insurgents: the district battalions of the civic militia, trade-guard bands, peasants and labourers streaming in from the provinces, and political refugees returning from exile. After the Tuileries fell, a provisional government was formed from Dupont de l'Eure, Cremieux, Arago, Lamartine, Dufaure, Bedeau and Cavaignac; after the June days Cavaignac held real power, running the capital with army infantry and the artillery of the forts. Command was personal rather than institutional, orders travelled by hand, and no staff existed to convert a street fight into a battle.
people: 路易·菲利浦在位十八年，二月革命時已七十五歲，倚賴總理大臣基佐與巴黎國民衛隊維持秩序，二十四日出走時連印章與文件都沒帶走，隨後流亡英國，此後再未回國。巴黎國民衛隊的靈魂人物是拉莫里西耶爾，他在一月二十三日拒絕用國民衛隊去驅散支持政府的人群，被人稱為「老虎」；革命後他率國民衛隊巡邏，又在六月的制憲會議上痛斥政府槍殺，主動辭去軍職。佩迪耶掌握民兵砲隊，二十四日在市政廳一帶的砲火是王朝覆亡的關鍵。卡瓦IGNAC原本是將軍而非革命者，他在六月二十三日出任陸軍大臣兼巴黎軍區司令，用密集砲火逐段掃清街壘，之後以軍事權力主導第二共和國，隨後當選立法會議主席。共和派領袖克雷米歐以「不可敗者」著稱，主持了四月的選舉與新憲法的起草。拉多里基-羅蘭、阿拉戈與拉馬丁分掌內政、司法與外交，奠定共和的行政框架。工人方面，國民工場的技術工人與聖安東尼區的木匠是街壘的主要修築者；制憲會議在六月重組投票資格後，工人階級的選票被大幅削減，直接引發了六月暴動。
peopleEn: Louis-Philippe, seventy-five years old when the monarchy collapsed, leaned on Prime Minister Guizot and the National Guard of Paris to keep order; on the twenty-fourth he left without his papers or his seal, crossed to England and never came back. The central figure of the National Guard was General Lamoriciere, who on 23 January refused to use the citizen battalions against a crowd supporting the government and was known as the Tiger; after the revolution he led patrols through the capital, and in June he denounced the shootings from the tribune of the Constituent Assembly before resigning his command. Pedier commanded the citizen artillery, and the guns firing around the Hotel de Ville on the twenty-fourth did much to settle the question of the crown. Cavaignac, a soldier rather than a revolutionary, became minister of war and commander of the Seine on 23 June, broke the barricades with concentrated artillery, and thereafter governed the republic through the army before presiding over the assembly. Cremieux, the incorruptible, ran the April elections and the drafting of the new constitution; Ledru-Rollin, Arago and Lamartine took charge of the interior, justice and foreign affairs and gave the republic its administrative frame. On the labour side the joiners of the National Workshops and the carpenters of the Faubourg Saint-Antoine built the barricades, and when the assembly rewrote the electoral law in June the workers' vote was gutted, which is what turned the June insurrection.
kits: 軍隊的骨幹是法軍一八四〇年制式步槍，雷管擊發，十四點七毫米口徑，配紙殼彈與刺刀；步槍手排成連縱隊，射擊靠齊射的訓令而非個人瞄準。巴黎國民衛隊與起義者手上的武器則極不統一：工廠繳出的舊式燧發火槍、私人買來的獵槍與卡賓槍、口徑各異的滑膛手槍，還有一八四八年三月一日新法要求登記的私人槍械，登記數以十萬計，卻多數無從校正。砲兵方面，市政廳與巴士底一帶的民兵用舊式攻城砲改裝的野砲與臼砲，火藥量與射程全靠經驗估算；騎兵只有馬刀與少量手槍。街壘的建材不是軍用品，而是石塊、鋪路石、馬車與門板，防守者居高臨下用獵槍射擊，使攻方的火槍精度無從發揮。巴士底獄廣場的武器庫被奪後，成箱的步槍與火藥被搬上街壘；到六月，街壘上的武器存量已足以裝備數萬人，但真正決定射程的仍是那批制式雷管步槍。
kitsEn: The backbone of the army was the French Model 1840 musket: percussion ignition, a calibre of 14.7 millimetres, paper cartridge, bayonet fixed. The musket was fought in files and by volley, and the drill taught soldiers to fire on command rather than to aim individually. In the hands of the National Guard and the insurgents the picture was anything but uniform. Old flintlock muskets taken from workshops, privately owned sporting guns, carbines and hand guns of every bore, and the private weapons registered after the law of 1 March 1848, which ran to hundreds of thousands, most of them useless for disciplined fire. The artillery was improvised: old siege pieces converted to field guns, mortars, and gun crews estimating range by eye. The barricades were built from street furniture rather than military stores, piles of paving stone, carts and doors, and their advantage came from height, since defenders with sporting guns could shoot down on a column that could only advance in single file. When the weapons of the Bastille were seized, boxes of muskets and powder went up to the barricades, and by June the arms stacked in the streets could have equipped tens of thousands, yet the range that decided fights still came from that batch of service percussion muskets.
tactics: 二月的攻防集中在巴黎東區的窄街與廣場。國民衛隊的資產階級營依據國民大會廣場與市政廳，王朝的常備軍與騎兵封鎖通往巴士底獄與聖安東尼區的道路。二十四日凌晨，攻擊者以大隊人潮沿里沃利大街推進，在杜伊勒里宮外與衛戍部隊逐段交鋒，守軍以刺刀與火槍守住院門，直到守備指揮官陣亡、宮門被衝開，王室成員分頭逃逸。三月二日，數萬名武裝者與國民衛隊在巴士底獄廣場集結、列隊，隊伍延伸到聖安東尼區，工人以木匠的手藝築起第一道街壘，用家具與石塊把街口封死。政府在三月十五日把常備軍撤出巴黎、又在五月十五日下令解散國民衛隊，等於把首都的武裝真空拱手讓給街壘。六月暴動時，鎮壓方改變打法：先用重砲在遠處對街壘逐段轟擊，再以步兵在掩護下推進，把守軍從缺口趕出，最後在巴士底一帶的窄街以密集射擊結束抵抗。防守方則反覆示範同一套辦法：把最窄的路口用石堆封死，用獵槍消耗進攻者的時間，等他們在煙霧中重新排隊。
tacticsEn: The fighting of February was fought in the narrow streets and squares of eastern Paris. The bourgeois battalions of the National Guard held the Place de la Bastille and the approaches to the Hotel de Ville, while royal regulars and cavalry sealed the roads to the Faubourg Saint-Antoine. In the early hours of the twenty-fourth, columns of people pushed up the Rue de Rivoli and fought house by house before the Tuileries, where the garrison answered with bayonets and musket fire until the officer commanding the defence was killed and the gates were forced; the royal family scattered in different directions. On 2 March tens of thousands of armed men and the National Guard were drawn up in the Place de la Bastille, the ranks stretching back into the Faubourg Saint-Antoine, and carpenters raised the first barricades out of furniture and stone. The government's errors were as important as the insurgents' skill: the regular army was withdrawn from Paris on 15 March, and on 15 May the National Guard was dissolved, leaving the capital's armed vacuum open to the barricades. When the June rising came, the method changed. Heavy guns opened at range, pounding the barricades section by section, and infantry advanced under cover, driving the defenders out of the gaps; the last resistance was broken with massed fire in the streets around the Place de la Bastille. The defenders had shown the same logic all along: narrow the street to its tightest point with stone, keep the sporting rifles busy, and make the attackers reform in the smoke before they came within reach.
data: 可以確定的數字大致如下。巴黎常備軍約一萬人，國民衛隊平時約二萬四千名，革命爆發後數週內湧入巴黎的武裝者以數萬計，軍械庫被奪的數量當時有數十箱之說，說法不一。國民工場於二月廿六日設立，到六月議會決議關閉之前，場內僱用了逾一萬名技師與零工，這個數字是理解六月暴動的直接背景。二月革命本身的死亡數遠小於六月：官方的死亡記錄以百計，其中二月廿四日攻入杜伊勒里宮一役與二十五日香榭麗舍大街方向的慘案佔大部分，二十五日一役的死亡人數在當時與後來都被認定為數百至上千，說法差異極大。六月暴動從廿三日到廿六日，官方公布的陣亡約一千五百人，被俘後被判刑者逾兩千人，其中正式執行槍決者約一千一百名，另有數百人流放。共和國成立後，全國範圍內要求登記的槍械數以十萬支計，多數為獵槍；軍費開支在半年內成倍上升，成為第二共和國最為人詬病的負擔之一。
dataEn: What can be stated with confidence is roughly this. Paris held about ten thousand regulars and a peacetime National Guard of some twenty-four thousand men; within weeks of the revolution the number of armed men converging on the capital ran into the tens of thousands, and the seizures of arms from the depots are counted in tens of boxes by one account and differently by another. The National Workshops were founded on 26 February and employed more than ten thousand artisans and labourers by the time the assembly voted them closed in June, a figure that explains the June rising directly. The deaths of February were far fewer than those of June: the official count runs to hundreds, most of them in the assault on the Tuileries on the twenty-fourth and in the slaughter of the crowd on the Champs-Elysees on the twenty-fifth, where contemporary and later estimates range from several hundred to a thousand dead. The June days, from the twenty-third to the twenty-sixth, produced an official death toll of about fifteen hundred, more than two thousand prisoners sentenced, roughly eleven hundred of them actually executed, and several hundred sent into exile. After the republic was proclaimed, the number of firearms declared across France passed two hundred thousand, most of them sporting guns, while military expenditure multiplied within six months and became one of the standing reproaches against the Second Republic.
cause: 直接觸發是一八四〇年代下半的歉收與糧價上漲，一八四七年巴黎的麵粉與麵包價格一度上漲數倍，手工業者與外省農工大批湧入首都。制度層面的不滿更為持久：國王在一八三〇年曾許諾逐步擴大選舉權，一八四二年修訂的選舉法卻只讓極少數富有的納稅人投票，天主教與自由派聯盟提出的改革要求屢遭拒絕。執政的基佐政府被批評為只維護資產階級利益、把持新聞檢查，自由派報紙被查封、記者被控，使改革議題在報紙上與街頭同時升溫。外患與外交的停滯同樣被歸咎於王朝：一八四八年二月巴黎的消息傳到維也納、柏林與那不勒斯，加劇了歐洲各處的緊張，讓國王的退位看來不可避免；而一八四七年西西里、拿不勒斯的起義，使法國的資產階級相信秩序已經崩解，必須靠武裝與街壘換取選票與政治機會。共和派並非二月才出現，一八三〇年之後他們在國民大會的選舉裡已屢次贏得席位；但直到王朝軍隊與國民衛隊在街上互相對峙，二月的街壘才把長年的憲政爭議變成一次可以見血的對決。
causeEn: The immediate trigger was the poor harvests of the later 1840s and the sharp rise in the price of bread; in 1847 the price of flour and bread in Paris rose several times over, and artisans and rural labourers poured into the capital. The structural grievances ran deeper. The king had promised in 1830 to widen the suffrage, yet the electoral law revised in 1842 left the vote with a small body of rich taxpayers, and the demands of the Catholic and liberal alliance were refused again and again. The government of Guizot was blamed for serving propertied interests alone and for clamping down on the press: reform papers were seized and journalists prosecuted, which drove the argument onto the streets and into the columns at the same time. Its foreign policy was equally blamed for standing still. When news of Paris reached Vienna, Berlin and Naples in February 1848 the tension rose everywhere, and the king's fall looked inevitable; the risings in Sicily and Naples in 1847 had already convinced the French bourgeoisie that the old order was cracking, and that arms and barricades were the currency in which a claim on the vote and on power would be bought. The republicans were not new: they had won seats at the National Assembly elections after 1830. But only when the royal troops and the National Guard faced each other in the street did a constitutional argument become a fight that could be settled in blood.
impact: 二月革命把法國從君主立憲推到共和，也把歐洲推入一八四八年革命的連鎖反應。共和國存在的第一年就顯示出它的脆弱：總統與議會互相猜忌，總統府遷入凡爾賽，軍隊被視為共和的敵人，首都成為政治鬥爭的競技場。六月鎮壓在政治上救了共和國，卻在社會上留下更深的裂痕：流亡者與被放逐者累積，工人與共和派互相怨懟，壓制工人的傳統成為第二共和國的既定政策。對外方面，共和政府改變了王朝對歐洲革命的冷淡態度，法國軍隊先後介入羅馬與義大利，鎮壓一八四九年的羅馬共和國，以秩序為名的國際觀由此成形。最具決定性的影響發生在一八五一年十二月二日：拿破崙三世與軍方以政變解散國民大會、恢復帝制，共和國只存在了四年；而二月革命所釋放的武裝群眾與政治熱情，反而在隨後數十年裡被移到帝制的對外戰爭上，用在克里米亞與索馬里。當年街壘上的雷管步槍，在六月的密集射擊裡被推到射程極限，最終決定了巴黎的歸屬。
impactEn: The February revolution carried France from constitutional monarchy to a republic and set Europe cascading into the revolutions of 1848. The republic's first year showed how fragile it was: the executive and the assembly distrusted each other, the presidency moved to Versailles, and the army was treated as the republic's enemy, so that the capital became the arena of political struggle. The June repression saved the republic politically and deepened the social wound: exiles and deportations accumulated, workers and republicans grew to distrust one another, and the suppression of the workers became a standing policy of the Second Republic. Abroad, the republic replaced the monarchy's cold shoulder to European revolutions; French troops intervened in Rome and Italy, crushed the Roman Republic of 1849, and the international order built on that intervention took shape. The decisive consequence came on 2 December 1851, when Napoleon III and the army dissolved the National Assembly and restored empire, so that the republic lasted barely four years. The armed crowds and political energy released in February were instead channeled into the external wars of the empire, at Crimea and beyond, and the percussion muskets that had fought from the barricades in June, pushed to the limit of their range by massed fire, had already decided the fate of Paris.
result: 二月廿二日王朝軍隊開槍，二十三日國民衛隊與民眾反擊，廿四日杜伊勒里宮被攻破，路易·菲利浦出逃英國，臨時政府當夜在巴黎市政廳宣告共和成立。共和並未帶來秩序：四月選舉與制憲會議之後，五月十五日政府下令解散國民衛兵，把武裝從合法的國民手中收回，六月廿一日議會又決定關閉國民工場，工人當即起義並在巴士底與聖安東尼區築起數十道街壘。廿三日到廿六日，卡瓦IGNAC指揮的陸軍以砲火與步兵攻破街壘，起義被平定，領袖遭槍決與流放，國民工場改由私人承包，工人失去保障。第二共和國於是成立，並在四年間維持了由軍方主導的秩序。整場衝突的結果是：王朝崩潰、君主制退場、共和制度確立，同時也把軍隊變成共和國的仲裁者，後來的政變與第二帝國由此預先寫好。
resultEn: Royal troops fired on 22 February, the National Guard and the crowds answered on the twenty-third, the Tuileries were stormed on the twenty-fourth, and Louis-Philippe left for England; the provisional government proclaimed the republic that night at the Hotel de Ville. The republic brought no order. After the April elections and the Constituent Assembly, the government dissolved the National Guard on 15 May, taking arms out of lawful citizens' hands, and on 21 June the assembly voted to close the National Workshops; workers rose at once and built dozens of barricades in the Faubourg Saint-Antoine. Between the twenty-third and the twenty-sixth Cavaignac's troops broke them with artillery and infantry, the leaders were shot or exiled, and the workshops passed into private hands. The Second Republic was born with the army as its referee, and the coup and the Second Empire were written into that arrangement well in advance. The outcome of the whole affair was this: the monarchy collapsed, constitutional monarchy gave way to a republic, and the armed force that had decided the barricades became the arbiter of the new order.
